definitions.gloss: bare feet; barefoot; without socks or stockings
definitions.explanation: Feet without any covering such as socks, stockings, or shoes. In Japanese culture, being barefoot indoors is common, but going barefoot outdoors or in formal situations is notable.

examples.japanese: {素足|すあし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧。
⟦{夏|なつ}→夏：02236_natsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{素足|すあし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦サンダル→サンダル：01365_sandaru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{気持|きも}ちいい→気持ちいい：09583_kimochiii⟧。
examples.english: In summer, sandals on bare feet feel nice.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{素足|すあし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{砂浜|すなはま}→砂浜：12333_sunahama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{駆|か}け{回|まわ}っていた→駆け回る：06113_kakemawaru⟧。
examples.english: The children were running around the sandy beach barefoot.

notes:
USAGE:
{素足|すあし} refers specifically to feet without socks or stockings. It can be used adverbially with the particle で ({素足|すあし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ = barefoot).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {素足|すあし}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{歩|ある}く→歩く：00538_aruku⟧ (to walk barefoot)
- {素足|すあし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦サンダル→サンダル：01365_sandaru⟧ (sandals on bare feet)
- {素足|すあし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧まま (still barefoot)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{裸足|はだし}→裸足：17169_hadashi⟧ also means barefoot but emphasizes having no shoes at all. {素足|すあし} specifically means without socks or stockings, and can include wearing shoes directly on bare feet.
